newsitem.title: GERMANY: Swissair German cargo volume to rise 5pct.
newsitem.headline: Swissair German cargo volume to rise 5pct.

text.p: Swissair cargo manager, Germany, Urs Steinmann said he expects to achieve an ex-Germany cargo throughput of about 54,000 tonnes this year, a rise of up to five percent on 1995.
Swissair trucks up to 90 percent of its Germany freight on daily overnight services to Switzerland, using Georg Reischel Luftfracht GmbH, he told Reuters in an interview.
"We reach the entire network on the next day. This allows us to sell at a higher price level(than the market average), at or slightly under Lufthansa Cargo AG prices," he said.
Swissair Germany has fixed allotments on ex-Zurich freighter and passenger services, and currently only charges customers for space used rather than space ordered, he noted.
The airline also deliberately makes sure it does not over-book, thus keeping the load factor lower than with other airlines, he pointed out.

Questioned whether Swissair plans to sell its services directly to air cargo shippers, Steinmann stressed: "We work only with forwarders. We have no strategy to sell directly to clients." --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 8982 Fax +44 171 542 5017
